title: Add integration test for KV/prefix cache metrics (hit/miss + miss reasons)
author: Samir Qureshi
body: ## Summary Adds an integration test that drives repeated prompts through the real prefill/decode request path and asserts that cache metrics move in the expected direction (miss on first request, hit/partial hit on subsequent requests). This is meant to be a guardrail against regressions in hit attribution (especially around continuous batching and request retries) and to validate the metric wiring end-to-end (runtime -> metrics recorder).  ## Motivation Unit tests validate individual counters/histograms, but we’ve already hit a few integration-level failure modes during implementation (metrics not tagged due to missing context, counters double-counted across retries, test-only metric registry not isolated). This adds a single “golden path” integration test that is deterministic and cheap to run in CI.  ## What the test does - Spins up the runtime integration harness with cache enabled and telemetry sampling forced to 1.0 for the test process. - Uses a fixed model fixture (small, deterministic) and a fixed prompt seed so tokenization is stable. - Executes a sequence: (1) request A (baseline miss), (2) identical request A (expected hit), (3) request A with a small suffix (expected partial hit / reuse), (4) request B (new prefix, expected miss). - Captures metrics from the in-process metrics sink and asserts:   - `cache.kv.requests_total{result="miss"}` increments on the first request, then `result="hit"` increments on the second identical request.   - Miss reason taxonomy is populated (for the baseline miss we assert `reason="cold"` or `reason="not_found"` depending on build flags; see notes below).   - Prefix reuse histogram has non-zero count on the suffix case (we don’t assert exact bucket, only that a reuse observation was recorded and reused_tokens > 0).   - No double counting on the retry path: the test can optionally enable one forced retry; we assert counters only increment once per logical request when `x-redwood-retry-attempt` is present.  ## Implementation notes - Introduces a `TestMetricsRecorder` that plugs into the existing metrics facade and exports a snapshot for assertions. This avoids scraping Prometheus in CI and avoids high-cardinality label assertions. - Test explicitly disables background flush timers and uses a synchronous flush hook before reading the snapshot to remove timing flakiness. - Uses coarse assertions (delta-based) and avoids asserting on model/route labels to keep the test stable while tag allowlists evolve.  ## CI/Perf - Adds ~0.8s to the runtime integration test suite on my laptop, ~1.4s in CI (cold). - No production code path changes beyond a small test-only constructor wiring under `#[cfg(test)]`.  ## Checklist - [x] Deterministic (no wall-clock sleeps; explicit flush) - [x] No raw prompt logging in test output (only prompt id and token counts) - [x] Validates both hit/miss and at least one “reuse depth” signal - [x] Works with continuous batching enabled in CI config  ## Follow-ups - We should add a second test case for batched prefill hit attribution once PR-18433 lands; this test is intentionally single-threaded to be deterministic. - Once metric names are finalized via naming standards, we can tighten the assertions to match the final names (right now we reference the runtime facade constants to avoid brittle string matches).
commits: test(runtime/cache): add integration test harness helper for metrics snapshot
test(runtime/cache): add kv/prefix cache hit/miss integration test
runtime(metrics): expose synchronous flush hook for tests only
test: fix flake by isolating global metrics registry per test
conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): This is the right shape. Two asks: (1) please avoid asserting specific miss reason values until the taxonomy stabilizes; we’ve got ongoing debate in #eng-runtime. (2) make sure this doesn’t rely on background export intervals — we’ve been burned by flakes.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. Updated to assert only that exactly one miss reason label is present (non-empty) and that total miss count increments by 1. Also added `flush_metrics_for_test()` and removed the `sleep(200ms)` I originally had.

Nadia Rahman (review): Can you ensure the test doesn’t introduce per-request labels in the snapshot (prompt hash, request id, etc.)? We’ve got cardinality guards coming on the ingestion side; we shouldn’t normalize on those labels in runtime tests either.

Samir Qureshi (author): Confirmed we only read the aggregate counters emitted by the runtime facade (no request id labels). The `TestMetricsRecorder` drops unknown labels by default and will fail the test if a forbidden label key shows up.

Noah Patel (review): One more thing: the second identical request may still miss if the harness tears down the model between calls. I think your harness resets state on each request right now. Please double check it’s reusing the same runtime instance and cache.
Samir Qureshi (author): Great catch — the harness was creating a fresh engine per request in this test. Fixed to keep a single runtime instance for the whole test and added a comment explaining why.

Sofia Ivanova (review): This is fine from scheduling’s perspective. Thanks for keeping it single-threaded. Approving as long as we don’t pin exact bucket indices for reuse depth (those change as we tune buckets).
Omar El-Sayed (approval): LGTM after the flush + harness reuse fix. This should protect us against the retry/double-counting class of bugs.
ci_summary: Buildkite: runtime-unit-tests (pass), runtime-integration-tests (pass), clippy (pass), fmt (pass). Initial run failed once due to a race reading metrics before export; resolved by synchronous flush and registry isolation.
release_notes: Internal: adds CI integration coverage for cache hit/miss metric correctness; no user-visible behavior change.
